title: The norm characteristic polynomial for a finite locally free affine algebra
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital ring homomorphism, and suppose the affine morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is finite locally free of degree $r\ge0$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $N_\varphi:B\to A$ denote the canonical determinant norm, characterized by the determinant of the multiplication matrix on every local finite free chart. Write $\varphi[T]:A[T]\to B[T]$ for its coefficientwise polynomial extension [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The latter map is finite locally free of degree $r$ as well. For $b\in B$, put
$$
P_b(T)=N_{\varphi[T]}(T-b)\in A[T].
$$
This polynomial has the form $T^r+\sum_{j<r}a_jT^j$ with $a_j\in A$ and satisfies $\bigl(\varphi[T](P_b)\bigr)(b)=0$ in $B$. In particular it is monic of degree $r$ when $A\ne0$. If $A$ is the zero ring, the displayed form and annihilation assertion still hold. The norm and polynomial are defined by the local determinant characterization, independent of choices of local bases. No global freeness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 02DU (exercises-exercise-trace-det)(1), 02DV (exercises-exercise-trace-det-rings)(1),(3), and 00DX (algebra-lemma-charpoly), applied on local finite free charts; the same norm polynomial is used in groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants.

proof.text: First suppose $A=0$. Since $\varphi$ is unital, $1_B=\varphi(1_A)=\varphi(0_A)=0_B$, so $B=0$ too. Both polynomial rings are zero rings. There is a unique function $B\to A$ and a unique function $B[T]\to A[T]$; these satisfy every local determinant condition, since their spectra have no points. The polynomial extension has empty source and target, so the finite, flat, locally finitely presented and fibre-degree conditions are vacuous. Its unique polynomial equals $T^r+\sum_{j<r}0T^j$, and its value at the unique element of $B$ is zero. Henceforth assume $A\ne0$.

source.place: Tags 02DU and 02DV: empty-spectrum case of the determinant construction

proof.text: Let $f:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $E=f_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$. The hypotheses of [def-pc-finite-locally-free] give finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation. The rank in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso] is explicitly the residue-field dimension in our degree hypothesis, hence is $r$ everywhere. Apply [lem-sc-finite-pushforward-rank-on-open] to the whole target. Thus $E$ is locally free of constant rank $r$. In the meaning of [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], choose a trivializing open cover $V_a$ with $E|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus r}$; $E$ is quasi-coherent. The structure sheaf is itself locally free of rank one, so it too is quasi-coherent.

Refine the $V_a$ by the principal-open basis of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], choose a finite subcover $D(f_1),\ldots,D(f_m)$; the $f_i$ generate the unit ideal. Discard empty members. To identify the sections on these opens, apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-basic-open-localization] to $F=E$ and $F=\mathcal O$ on the affine whole target. Since $f_i|_{D(f_i)}$ is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function], the map $F(X)_{f_i}\to F(D(f_i))$, $t/f_i^n\mapsto f_i^{-n}t|_{D(f_i)}$, exists. Clause (1) gives surjectivity, and clause (2) gives injectivity: a fraction with zero image has $f_i^kt=0$ for some $k$, hence is zero. Thus $\mathcal O(D(f_i))=A_{f_i}$ and $E(D(f_i))=B_{f_i}$ canonically, with scalar actions respected. Restrict the chosen sheaf trivialization to $D(f_i)$ and take sections; finite tuples of sections are the sections of a finite direct sum, so $B_{f_i}\cong A_{f_i}^{\oplus r}$.

source.place: Tags 00E0, 00E4, 00E8, 01IA and 01HZ; explicit localization argument also in WeilConjectures/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Tilde.lean, isLocalizedModule_Away

proof.text: The ring isomorphism $B\otimes_A A[T]\cong B[T]$ sends $b\otimes\sum_j a_jT^j$ to $\sum_j b\varphi(a_j)T^j$; its inverse sends $\sum_j b_jT^j$ to $\sum_j b_j\otimes T^j$. The tensor relations and coefficientwise polynomial operations show these are inverse ring homomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the polynomial extension on spectra is therefore the base change of $f$ along $\operatorname{Spec}A[T]\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Its rank at every point is $r$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso](2). Hence it is finite locally free of degree $r$ in the required sense. Applying [lem-sc-finite-pushforward-rank-on-open] also to this morphism makes its structure-sheaf pushforward locally free of rank $r$, hence quasi-coherent by [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module].

source.place: Tags 01I4, 01WL, 01U9, 01TS, 02KD and 04MH; explicit polynomial tensor isomorphism

proof.text: Put $g_i=C(f_i)\in A[T]$. They generate the unit ideal because an equality $\sum_i u_if_i=1$ maps to $\sum_i C(u_i)g_i=1$. There are canonical isomorphisms $A[T]_{g_i}\cong A_{f_i}[T]$ and $B[T]_{g_i}\cong B_{f_i}[T]$: send a polynomial divided by $f_i^n$ to its coefficientwise fractions. Conversely a polynomial with finitely many fractional coefficients has a common denominator $f_i^N$, where $N$ is the largest of their exponents. The localization relations show the maps are well-defined and inverse. If $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ is the basis in step 3, its constant polynomials form a basis of $B_{f_i}[T]$: expand each coefficient uniquely in the $e_k$ and gather the coefficient polynomials for each $k$. Thus both pairs $(A,B)$ and $(A[T],B[T])$ have finite principal covers with free module rank $r$.

source.place: Tag 02DV(3), polynomial base change: explicit common-denominator and coefficient-basis calculation

proof.text: For either pair $(R,D)=(A,B)$ or $(A[T],B[T])$ and each $u\in D$, let $\mu_u:D\to D$ be multiplication by $u$, an $R$-linear endomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence] to the cover just obtained, using a separate indeterminate $Z$. It gives a unique $\chi_u(Z)\in R[Z]$ characterized by its matrix characteristic polynomial after every scalar extension making $D$ free of rank $r$, and with the form $Z^r+\sum_{j<r}c_jZ^j$. In particular, on our localization charts it is $\det(ZI_r-M_i(u))$. The localization of $\mu_u$ is indeed multiplication by $u/1$: this follows either directly on fractions or from the naturality assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor].

Define the determinant norm on either pair by the real construction $N_{D/R}(u)=(-1)^r\chi_u(0)$. On any free scalar-extension chart its value is $(-1)^r\det(-M(u))=\det M(u)$: each term of the determinant permutation sum has exactly $r$ matrix entries, so replacing $M$ by $-M$ multiplies the determinant by $(-1)^r$. This is the determinant of multiplication in [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. It is independent of the basis by [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties](a). It also has this description on every affine open where the algebra is free of rank $r$: the canonical section identification with scalar extension is [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change], applied to the quasi-coherent pushforward of step 2 (and to the quasi-coherent polynomial pushforward established in step 4). The characterization in step 6 then applies. Any other proposed norm with this local characterization has the same image in every $R_{f_i}$ (or $R_{g_i}$); [lem-weil-pbc-standard-covering-glue](i) makes the values equal in $R$. This constructs precisely the norms in the statement, with no choice of global basis.

Fix $b\in B$ and let $M_i$ be the matrix of multiplication by $b/1$ on the basis of $B_{f_i}$. In the constant polynomial basis of step 5, multiplication by $T-b/1$ has matrix $TI_r-M_i$, since $(T-b/1)e_k=Te_k-\sum_l(M_i)_{lk}e_l$. Therefore the local determinant characterization of step 7 gives $P_b|_{A_{f_i}[T]}=\det(TI_r-M_i)$. On the other hand, this is exactly the localization of $\chi_b(T)$ from step 6. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-standard-covering-glue](i) to each coefficient of $P_b-\chi_b$ in $A$. All these coefficients vanish, so $P_b=\chi_b=T^r+\sum_{j<r}a_jT^j$. As $A\ne0$, its coefficient of $T^r$ is the nonzero element $1_A$ and its higher coefficients are zero, proving monicity and degree exactly $r$.

source.place: Tags 02DV(1), 00EJ; groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants, norm polynomial and its leading coefficient

proof.text: Every retained $D(f_i)$ is nonempty, hence $A_{f_i}\ne0$. Apply [lem-weil-cayley-hamilton-free-module] over $A_{f_i}$ to $\mu_{b/1}$ on the free module $B_{f_i}$. With $a_r=1$ and the coefficient notation of step 8, it says $\sum_{j=0}^r(a_j/1)\mu_{b/1}^{\,j}=0$. Evaluate this equality of endomorphisms at $1_{B_{f_i}}$. Induction on $j$ gives $\mu_{b/1}^{\,j}(1)=(b/1)^j$ (including $j=0$), so $\sum_{j=0}^r\varphi_{f_i}(a_j/1)(b/1)^j=0$ in $B_{f_i}$. This is exactly the localization of $\sum_{j=0}^r\varphi(a_j)b^j$, by the fraction formulas for addition and multiplication.

Apply the injectivity clause of [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact] to the $A$-module $M=B$ and the unit-ideal family $f_i$. Step 9 shows that $z=\sum_{j=0}^r\varphi(a_j)b^j$ maps to zero in each $B_{f_i}$, hence $z=0$ in $B$. By the definitions of polynomial coefficient extension and evaluation, this is $(\varphi[T](P_b))(b)=0$. If $r=0$, every $B_{f_i}$ is the zero module, so the same injectivity makes $B=0$; the empty determinant is $1_A$, $P_b=1_A$, and its evaluation in $B$ is zero. Thus rank zero, the empty basis, nonfaithful $A\to B$, and non-Noetherian rings are all included; the zero base ring was handled separately in step 1.

tool_uses.why: Converts the given constant fibre degree to a fixed-rank local trivialization of the finite algebra; a generic affine-geometric tool, not a replacement for the unit route.
Its two fraction assertions identify sections on the chosen principal opens with B localized as an A-module, without assuming Noetherianity.
Only clause (3), stability of local finite presentation under base change, is used for the polynomial morphism.
The already closed gluing interface constructs a characteristic polynomial from finite principal free charts; no Henselian-pair hypothesis is used.
Identifies affine free section charts with scalar extension, so the universal locally free characteristic-polynomial characterization applies.
Only injectivity on a finite principal cover is used to descend the locally zero element from B_fi to B.

lean.statement: theorem finiteLocallyFree_norm_characteristicPolynomial {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (r : ℕ) (h : (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree r) : (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Polynomial.mapRingHom φ))).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree r ∧ ∃ N : B → A, (IsLocallyFreeDeterminantNorm φ N ∧ ∀ N' : B → A, IsLocallyFreeDeterminantNorm φ N' → N' = N) ∧ ∃ Npoly : Polynomial B → Polynomial A, (IsLocallyFreeDeterminantNorm (Polynomial.mapRingHom φ) Npoly ∧ ∀ Npoly' : Polynomial B → Polynomial A, IsLocallyFreeDeterminantNorm (Polynomial.mapRingHom φ) Npoly' → Npoly' = Npoly) ∧ ∀ b : B, (∃ a : Fin r → A, Npoly (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b) = Polynomial.X ^ r + ∑ j : Fin r, Polynomial.C (a j) * Polynomial.X ^ (j : ℕ)) ∧ (Polynomial.map φ (Npoly (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b))).eval b = 0 ∧ (Nontrivial A → (Npoly (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b)).Monic ∧ (Npoly (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b)).natDegree = r)
lean.note: The theorem spells out unique existence of both norms from their local determinant characterization, together with polynomial base change, expansion, annihilation, and conditional monicity/degree. The two following definitions choose only these uniquely determined norm functions and form N_{φ[X]}(X-C b). The local determinant predicate is a helper for this owning node, not a replacement for the finite locally free hypothesis.
